newsitem.title: EGYPT: Investor bids cover Cairo Housing offer.
newsitem.headline: Investor bids cover Cairo Housing offer.

text.p: The Egyptian state's offer of at least 20 percent in partly-privatised Cairo Housing and Development has ended oversubscribed, the agent handling the privatisation said on Wednesday.

Mohammed Hossny, vice president of Triple A Securities, told Reuters there was high demand to buy the 1.272 million shares but he could not say by how much the offer was covered as brokers continued to tally the orders.
"The numbers we have so far show that it's oversubscribed but until they are final we can't say by how much," he said.
The state's Holding Company for Housing, Tourism and Cinema, which owns a 65 percent majority in Cairo Housing, offered investors part of its stake for five days from March 12.

It set the minimum share price at 24.72 pounds -- the stock's closing level on March 11 -- and Mohammed Abdel Salam, head of the bourse's clearing company said the final selling price would be decided by the price discovery mechanism.
"The offer is comfortably covered. It's possible the state will increase the number of shares on offer," Abdel Salam said.
The holding company said new shareholders would receive the 1996/97 dividend of 1.00 pound per share. The firm distributed 0.53 pounds in 95/96.

Real estate firms have proved popular with investors and their soaring share prices have helped fuel the bourse's recent record highs. Last May, the state sold off 70 percent of Medinet Nasr for 65 pounds a share and the stock was trading on Sunday at 517.70.

Brokers had said in July that privatised realty rival Medinet Nasr Housing and Development had bought out the holding company's stake but then the deal was refused. The state then said it would offer a 40 percent stake in the firm late last year but then changed its mind.
